newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos says economic growth on track.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos says economic growth on track.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Monday assured investors, who were last week pulling out of the country's stock market in droves, that the economy remained on its upward path.
"Don't be tense. Just relax...the forecast for all of 1997 is very well on track," Ramos said in his news conference.

The National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) is the agency tasked to monitor all economic indicators including the gross national product and gross domestic product which are due to be released later in the month.

Recent foreign investor share selling turned almost into a rout last week as they began to lose faith in the economy's prospects as more and more companies turned in disappointing profit figures for the first quarter of the year.
Ramos said analysts should not just focus on net income results, because many companies have spent most of their revenues to finance their expansion programmes.

The stock market finally ended its six days of sharp falls on plunging, rising just over five percent on Monday though traders were far from confident it marked the turnaround of the market's fortunes.
